name: Cuban Dominoes
description: Partnership block domino game for four players using a double-nine set of 55 tiles. Partners sit opposite; play proceeds counter-clockwise. Players add tiles to a line matching ends; first to empty hand or lowest pips when blocked wins the round. First team to 100 points wins the game.

history.origins: Cuban dominoes originated in Cuba; the principal form is partnership dominoes (Dominó de Parejas) for four players using a double-nine set, played with great enthusiasm.
timeline: 20th century: Cuban partnership dominoes (Dominó de Parejas) widely played with double-nine set.

setup.players: Four players in two partnerships; partners sit opposite.
setup.dealing: Tiles are mixed face down (darle agua). Each player in turn draws 10 tiles and places them on their rack hidden from others. The remaining 15 tiles stay face down and are not used during the round. Before the first deal, one player from each team draws a tile at random; the team whose tile has more spots plays first.
setup.equipment: 55 tiles; each player typically has a rack.

rules.objective: As a team, score points by winning rounds (emptying your hand or having the lowest pip count when the round is blocked). The first team to reach a cumulative score of 100 or more wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Tiles are played to form a line; touching ends of adjacent tiles must match. Doubles are played across the line at right angles; the line may turn corners. The first player may play any tile. Play continues counter-clockwise. On your turn you must add one tile to the line if you can; if you have no tile matching either open end you must pass. A round ends when one player plays their last tile (dominar or pegarse) or when the round is blocked (trancado): all four have tiles but none can play. When blocked, the player with fewest pips on remaining tiles wins the round. The winning team scores the total pips on the opponents' remaining tiles. The first team to 100 wins.
keyRules: Match touching ends on the line; doubles play across.
Play or pass each turn; no drawing during play.
Round ends when one empties hand or round is blocked (lowest pips wins).
Winning team scores opponents' remaining pips; first to 100 wins game.

scoring.description: Cumulative score per team. Winning team scores the total pips on the opponents' remaining tiles. First team to 100 or more wins the game.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach a cumulative score of 100 or more points wins the game. Round winner is the first to empty hand or, when blocked, the player with fewest pips on remaining tiles.

synthesis.shortDescription: Partnership block dominoes for four with double-nine set; play or pass to the line; first team to 100 wins.
